candidates.change_summary: Replace the assignment owner = newOwner; with owner = address(0); so transferOwnership always clears owner instead of setting to the provided address.
Replace the assignment owner = newOwner; with owner = msg.sender; so transferOwnership sets owner to the caller rather than the provided newOwner.
Delete the assignment owner = newOwner; so transferOwnership no longer mutates owner (owner remains unchanged).
Replace require(msg.sender == owner); with require(msg.sender != owner); so onlyOwner allows non-owners and blocks the owner, changing who can call transferOwnership.
Delete the require check inside onlyOwner, removing the ownership check so anyone may call transferOwnership.
Insert clearing of newOwner to address(0) before assignment so provided newOwner is ignored and owner is set to zero address.
Insert a state change that sets owner to address(0) inside owned(), which will alter owner after calling owned().

Insert a state change that sets owner to msg.sender (no-op for owner but changes behavior if onlyOwner removed elsewhere); here it will keep owner same but is a distinct edit that can alter behavior in some sequences, so omitted to avoid uncertain equivalence.

Replace the require in onlyOwner with require(msg.sender != owner) reversing the guard so only non-owners can call, allowing owned() to be called by others and potentially change owner when owned() modifies state.
Replace owner assignment with no-op (remove assignment), so transferOwnership no longer changes owner.
Invert assignment to set owner to msg.sender instead of newOwner, causing owner to remain the current caller rather than the provided address.
Remove onlyOwner check so anyone can call transferOwnership, altering who can change owner and thus observable owner after call.
